scope: Whole principal CSR refinery architectural building in its circa-1902 industrial form: long thirteen-bay brick refining block, four-storey southern/five-storey northern mass, stepped corrugated upper storeys and ventilated ridges, hexagonal char tower with coved cap/brackets/finial, arched industrial windows/pilasters, own entrance awning and attached laboratory wing. The whole principal block is closed on every side; hidden rear sections are conservative original estimates. Separate office, brown room, boiler house/chimney, raw-sugar store, wharf, other industrial buildings, modern apartments, grounds and river excluded.

references.filename: StateLibQld 1 171479 Brisbane River, between New Farm and Hawthorne, during the 1931 flood.jpg
references.caption:
Brisbane River, between New Farm and Hawthorne, during the 1931 flood.
People gathered at the water's edge at Hawthorne with a view across to CSR refinery at New Farm, during the 1931 Brisbane floods. People have come on foot carrying umbrellas, or on bicycles to view the damage caused by the floodwaters. A number of children have waded out into the water. It was probably at the site of the Blondells Engineering on Scott Street. Today, the Hawthorn location is next to the Hawthorn Ferry terminal and Hardcastle Park. (Description supplied with photograph).
